title: Online Financial Calculator
description: Solve n, i, PV, PMT, FV, NPV, and IRR in an educational online financial calculator with shareable links and sign guidance.

method.title: How to read this.
method.text: TVM solves one variable at a time with payments at the beginning or end of the period. NPV discounts each flow by period, and IRR searches for the rate that brings NPV near zero.
method.privacy: Calculations run in the browser. Shared links expose entered values in the URL.

howToUse.title: How to use an online financial calculator
howToUse.p1: Choose TVM or cash flows. In TVM, select the variable to solve and fill the rest using the same period unit.
howToUse.p2: For cash flows, place the investment or initial outflow in period 0 and subsequent receipts or payments in order.

tvmVariables.title: What n, i, PV, PMT, and FV mean
tvmVariables.text: n is the number of periods, i is the rate per period, PV is present value, PMT is periodic payment, and FV is future value.

signs.title: How to use positive and negative signs
signs.text: Financial math uses signs to separate inflows and outflows. For example, a loan received can be positive and the payments negative.

npvIrr.title: NPV and IRR for periodic cash flows
npvIrr.text: NPV brings future flows to period 0 using the discount rate. IRR is the periodic rate that makes NPV close to zero.

q1.question: Is this an official HP 12C?
q1.answer: No. It is a generic online financial calculator with no affiliation, endorsement, logo, physical layout, or firmware emulation.

q2.question: Can I use it instead of a physical financial calculator?
q2.answer: You can check common TVM, NPV, and IRR formulas, but results may differ from physical calculators, spreadsheets, or banks due to rounding and conventions.

q3.question: Why do some values need to be negative?
q3.answer: Opposite signs represent opposite cash directions. Without them, some equations have no useful financial solution.

q4.question: Is the rate monthly or annual?
q4.answer: The rate is always per period. If n is in months, i must be monthly; if n is in years, i must be annual.

q5.question: Why might IRR not appear?
q5.answer: IRR requires at least one positive and one negative flow and may not converge, especially for non-conventional flows.

q6.question: What is the difference between NPV and IRR?
q6.answer: NPV shows money value discounted by the chosen rate. IRR shows the rate that would make NPV close to zero.
